item.description: The European Union has summoned Moscow's diplomatic envoy to Brussels in response to a Russian drone entering Romanian airspace last week. "We conveyed our strong condemnation of the intentional violation of the airspace of Romania," said a spokesman for EU chief diplomat Kaja Kallas on Tuesday.

item.title: Criminal gangs increasingly lure people to work in online scam centers, UN migration agency warns
item.description: The U.N.'s migration agency is warning that criminal networks have been trafficking hundreds of thousands of people — many of them educated English speakers — to work in online scam centers, and the caseload is growing. The International Organization for Migration says victims are often lured by fake job advertisements — mostly through social media — promising work abroad, only to get locked up, have their identity documents seized, and forced through violence, threats and “debt bondage” to participate in the online scams. “We’re seeing so many more of these cases emerge right now," IOM Director-General Amy Pope told reporters in Geneva on Tuesday.

item.title: Majdal Shams dedicates memorial park honoring 12 children killed in rocket attack
item.description: In addition to the 12 boys and girls, ages 10 to 16, who had been pronounced dead, thirty-four others were wounded as a result of the strike. A memorial ceremony was held in Majdal Shams on Monday evening to commemorate the 12 victims of the rocket fired at the village from Lebanon.

item.description: Australia is planning to build its first new oil refinery since 1965 after petrol stations ran dry earlier this year.

item.title: US Ebola patient discharged from Frankfurt hospital
item.description: A patient infected with Ebola was discharged in good health from Frankfurt University Hospital in Germany on Tuesday. The US national, who was working as a logistics specialist for an aid organization, contracted the virus in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

item.title: Italy's birth rate hits post-war low as economic fears put women off
item.description: Italy recorded fewer births last year than at any point since the end of World War II. The national statistics office in Rome reported on Tuesday that the number of births fell again to just 355,000 - down 3.

item.description: A confession video has been found on the deceased suspect's phone after the deadly Berlin Pride attack, a spokeswoman for Germany's Federal Public Prosecutor's Office said on Tuesday. item.title: Poland denies Putin's claim of territorial claims in western Ukraine
item.description: Warsaw has denied Russian President Vladimir Putin's assertion that it is laying claim to parts of western Ukraine. "Poland has not made any territorial claims against Ukraine, is not currently making any, and does not intend to do so in the future," the Polish Foreign Ministry stated on Tuesday.

item.title: UN chief makes rare Cyprus visit to help ease decades-old ethnic division
item.description: U.N. Secretary-General António Guterres on a rare visit to Cyprus said Tuesday he was demonstrating his commitment to resolving the island nation's decades-old ethnic division, even as expectations remain low for a speedy breakthrough leading to a peace accord. “I will do everything I can to support the Greek Cypriots and Turkish Cypriots in this very important moment," Guterres said after talks with Greek Cypriot President Nikos Christodoulides.

item.title: Gunmen kill high-ranking Taliban official in Afghanistan in rare targeted attack
item.description: Gunmen killed a high-ranking local Taliban official in Afghanistan’s northwestern province of Badakhshan on Tuesday in a rare targeted killing in the country. Two gunmen shot Zabihullah Amiri, Badakhshan’s director of information and culture, as he headed from a local district to the provincial capital Faizabad, the Information Ministry said in a statement.

item.title: South Korean officials order residents to evacuate after reported white phosphorus leak at US base
item.description: South Korean authorities on Tuesday briefly ordered civilians to evacuate after what they described as a white phosphorus leak at a U.S. military base near the capital, Seoul. Officials in the city of Pyeongtaek urged nearby residents to move to a safe location and avoid skin exposure after the leak at the Osan Air Base was detected at around 5 p.m. They lifted the evacuation order several hours later, saying decontamination work had been completed, according to text messages sent out by the city. In a statement, the U.S. 51st Fighter Wing did not mention a leakage of white phosphorus but said it established a 1,000-foot (300-meter) safety cordon around the base “due to a ground mishap and out of an abundance of caution” to protect the base and the local populace.

item.title: Unrelated video from Canada falsely linked to India's 'cockroach' protesters
item.description: Weeks of protests by the social media-driven Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) demanding educational reform culminated in the resignation of India's education minister, but a video purporting to show protesters dancing at the Jantar Mantar demonstration site in New Delhi is false. AFP geolocated the video and matched it to Kitsilano Beach in Vancouver, Canada.

item.title: Several feared trapped in collapsed shopping mall after Japan quake
item.description: Several people are trapped inside a shopping mall that partially collapsed in an explosion after a large 7.1-magnitude earthquake struck the Japanese city of Kumamoto on Tuesday, according to Japan’s public broadcaster NHK.
